text: 1.5. For my presentation today, I'd like to talk about globalization and the film industry. What is the first place that comes to mind when you think of films? Most likely, it's Hollywood in the United States. Hollywood is a neighborhood of Los Angeles in California and was originally an agricultural town. It wasn't until the early 1900s that filmmakers started moving in. Since then, Hollywood has become more and more famous for its big-budget films. However, film production is not just an American business, as production companies making films for their domestic markets exist all over the world. For example, another highly successful film industry is Bollywood in India. India actually makes more films each year than any other country, hundreds more than the U.S. Other countries have big film industries, too. Mexico is the third largest producer of films, only just behind the U.S. Japan is the fourth largest, making around 600 films each year. But even Hollywood itself has become more multinational. In 1991, Hollywood made around 30% of its money from sales of international cinema tickets. However, in 2023, Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning Part 1 made around $235 million in its first five days, but only around 34% of ticket sales came from domestic audiences in the U.S. The remaining 66% came from people watching the movie in different markets worldwide. Around 10% of international sales during this opening week, worth an astonishing $25 million, came from China alone. This is not surprising, given that China accounted for over $136 million worth of sales for a previous Mission Impossible film. Of course, many films which look like they're made in the U.S. aren't actually made there. Next time you watch a film with New York City as the location, just bear in mind that you may not be seeing New York at all. Because everything was filmed somewhere like Toronto or Vancouver in Canada. The number is so high that Canada has sometimes been called Hollywood North. The film industry adds over $9 billion Canadian dollars to that country's economy every year, providing work for a quarter of a million people. Why is this happening? The answer is mainly a financial one. Labor costs tend to be slightly higher in the U.S. than in Canada, where the cost of living tends to be slightly lower too. But there's another reason, and it's to do with the very generous tax discounts that the Canadian authorities give to filmmakers. Basically, film producers get tax credits, meaning that their taxes can be reduced by a certain percentage. Rules vary from place to place in Canada, but in British Columbia, where Vancouver is the biggest city, filmmakers can claim a basic tax credit of 35%, as well as a credit for the same amount for scriptwriting costs. A tax credit of 16% can also be claimed for the costs of making digital animation and visual effects. All of this, of course, brings people to work in places like Vancouver, staying in its hotels, eating in its restaurants, and contributing to its economy. Not only are filmmakers happy, but the profits of businesses in the city increase. In order to get these tax credits, though, you do need to be a business permanently established in Canada. Do you remember the Hollywood film Titanic? For that film, a large production set was actually built in Mexico. Since foreign films made in Mexico are considered exports, producers are free from having to pay certain types of tax, making Mexico an appealing location for filmmakers. And, of course, it brings jobs and money to Mexico. Consequently, it's a win-win for both sides. Another popular area for filming is the Middle East. For example, Hollywood has made films in the United Arab Emirates and Jordan. The reason for the popularity of these countries is similar. Tax incentives. In addition to great locations with sun, deserts, water, and cities, the United Arab Emirates offers a 30% rebate on production costs and even helps Hollywood organize permits, visas, customs clearance, and script approval. Jordan helps producers avoid taxes, such as the VAT, value-added tax, that is added to goods and services that are bought. Therefore, more and more films are being made there. In conclusion, the Hollywood film industry has become more and more globalized. Not only does it bring its films to viewers around the world, it is also bringing jobs and money into countries outside the United States.
